summary.tpReason: Falcon recorded jliu running `vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet` on srv-dc01, a destructive recovery-inhibition action consistent with ransomware preparation. Although this individual detection is labelled false_positive/dismissed, jliu was simultaneously tied to true-positive credential-dumping and malicious-execution detections on srv-file01 and it-ws01, making a benign explanation for the DC action less credible.
summary.fpReason: Falcon's final status for this exact detection is `false_positive`, and Sentinel marks the alert Dismissed. No Windows SecurityEvent telemetry corroborates the execution, and the process was launched under the interactive user jliu rather than an identified malware binary; an authorized shadow-copy cleanup remains possible.
summary.whatHappened: At 2026-08-15 14:48:39Z, Falcon detected jliu (jliu@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com) executing `C:\Windows\System32\vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet` on Windows Server 2022 domain controller srv-dc01 (PKWORK; 10.0.0.10; Falcon agent cs-aid-srvdc01-0006). The process chain was explorer.exe -> cmd.exe -> vssadmin.exe. Falcon reports the action as Blocked and Killed and Quarantined=true; the host was online at 15:35Z and not filesystem-contained. This occurred amid a 14:36–15:26Z multi-host sequence involving jliu, including true-positive LSASS dumping on srv-file01 (14:36Z) and it-ws01 (14:57Z), plus execution/staging alerts on it-ws01. The exact srv-dc01 detection was nevertheless labelled false_positive by Falcon and dismissed in Sentinel.
keyEvidence: CrowdStrikeDetections for srv-dc01 records vssadmin.exe with command `vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet` under jliu at 2026-08-15 14:48:39Z; its stated disposition is Blocked and Killed and Quarantined=true.
The srv-dc01 detection and CrowdStrikeAlerts record Falcon status `false_positive`; the corresponding Sentinel alert status is Dismissed. This is the principal benign/contrary indicator.

Correlated jliu detections show true-positive LSASS credential dumping on srv-file01 at 14:36:39Z and it-ws01 at 14:57:03Z, and malicious execution/file-staging activity on it-ws01 in the same time window.
CrowdStrikeHosts shows srv-dc01 was normal, managed, protected by a prevention policy, and not filesystem-contained at 15:35:27Z; the server remained online after the blocked process.
